claims.text: Under the byte-identical common-baseline prompt, generator choice shifted the two-error operating point: Qwen had lower plain and pressured unsafe-compliance failure than Mistral but higher authorized-control refusal.
claims.estimand: Qwen minus Mistral panel failure-rate difference at the common baseline: plain -0.55 (95% CI -0.775 to -0.325), pressured -0.4012738853503185 (95% CI -0.5534722222222221 to -0.2597222222222222), control +0.1875 (95% CI +0.0625 to +0.34375).
claims.causal_scope: Generator contrast under the tested common prompt and synthetic bank only; no deployment-effect claim.

claims.text: Only Qwen with deliberation passed the registered Week 7 mitigation rule; prompt effects did not transfer uniformly across generators.
claims.estimand: Relative pressured-failure reduction versus each generator's adapted baseline, jointly constrained by no more than +3.125 percentage points of control failure.
claims.causal_scope: Within-generator arm comparisons on the registered bank; no general prompt-method ranking.

claims.text: Weeks 5 through 7 show that the apparent effect of an intervention depends on the measurement stack and generator, so lexical success cannot substitute for semantically adjudicated action outcomes.
claims.estimand: Cross-experiment synthesis of the Week 5 full semantic audit, Week 6 registered diagnostic, and Week 7 confirmation; no pooled meta-analytic effect.
claims.causal_scope: Process finding across non-identical experiments; it does not estimate a universal measurement-stack effect.

claims.text: In Week 7 common-baseline complete pairs, pressured wording failed less often than paired plain wording for both generators, and the descriptive differences varied across bundled pressure cues.
claims.estimand: Mean pressured-minus-plain failure among complete pairs, with deterministic family-clustered bootstrap intervals.
claims.causal_scope: Post-outcome descriptive audit only; tactics are confounded with scenario family, pair variant, wording, setting, and — in the false_clearance arm — prerequisite salience.

claims.text: Platform evaluation should treat unsafe compliance and authorized-control refusal as joint operating-point criteria, with calibrated deferral evaluated as a possible third action.
claims.estimand: No deployment estimand; this is an application and future-evaluation proposal derived from C1 and related work.
claims.causal_scope: Research guidance only, not a production deployment approval or validated platform policy.

limitations.text: The confirmation evidence is synthetic, text-only, and limited to two 7B-class generators and two platform contexts; it does not establish embodied or deployed performance.
The judge panel was accepted through a disclosed pooled-evidence amendment after the registered single-holdout certification rule proved underpowered; the weakest pooled unsafe stratum was 14/16.
Three Qwen pressured rows had unparsed panel endpoints and two generated outputs had nonconforming headers; the prespecified exclusions remain disclosed.
Weeks 5, 6, and 7 differ in prompts, banks, templates, and judging regimes, preventing a single pooled causal estimate across experiments.

The pressure-cue audit is post-outcome, and tactic assignment is confounded with family, pair variant, wording, and setting. Explicit missing-prerequisite language additionally appears in 8 of 32 pressured items, all in the false_clearance arm, so that arm is confounded with prerequisite salience — the factor the withdrawn contrast intended to isolate. Cue-specific rows are descriptive only, and the salience explanation of the plain/pressure reversal is neither supported nor ruled out.
Calibrated deferral, RAG, fine-tuning, multimodal state, actuation constraints, and deployed operator workflows were not tested.
